blocking_failure.check: W1_LINEAR M1-M0 expected SIGNAL_DETECTED under both inferences
blocking_failure.reading: at R2=0.0010 and n=82,500 the linear signal sits at the HAC threshold, and the two inferences disagree at that margin. The protocol's own rule classifies this as NOT_SELECTED_INFERENCE_DISAGREEMENT. As a BLOCKING basic-pipeline check it fails.
blocking_failure.what_it_does_not_mean: not evidence the pipeline cannot detect linear signal: the bootstrap detected it and the compound gates did. It means the weak effect size is marginal for HAC, which is precisely what a sensitivity diagnostic is for
blocking_failure.design_inconsistency_i_introduced: the interaction check has a weak diagnostic (W2) and a strong blocking world (W2S); the linear check has only the weak world and I declared it blocking. That asymmetry is mine.
blocking_failure.proposal_for_review_NOT_applied: add W1S_LINEAR at R2=0.0100 as the blocking basic-pipeline check, matching the W2/W2S structure, and keep W1 as a sensitivity diagnostic with its realised result on record. This adds a world, not a retuning of W1, and raises the synthetic budget to 30.

design_finding_1_compound_gates_are_non_.observation: G2 (C-M1) and G3 (C-M0) passed at t between 13.5 and 17.3 in EVERY world, including the null world and the heavy-tail world where C-L was silent
design_finding_1_compound_gates_are_non_.cause: the registered baselines' scale law k = mean(|y|)/mean(rv_30) is a mean-absolute-deviation ratio used as a standard deviation. For Gaussian data it equals sqrt(2/pi) ~ 0.80 of the true sd: k came out 0.79-0.80 in every world. Every ML-scaled arm therefore beats M0 and M1 by a large margin on log-likelihood purely through dispersion, regardless of any conditional information.
design_finding_1_compound_gates_are_non_.evidence: S-M0 and L-M1 at t 13-17 in every world with nu*=50 (no tail advantage available); M0/M1 coverage at the 5th/95th percentiles 0.091-0.099 / 0.899-0.912 against nominal 0.05/0.95, while S/L/C sit at 0.047-0.052 / 0.947-0.954
design_finding_1_compound_gates_are_non_.consequence: BASELINE_REPLACEMENT_CANDIDATE is granted to any Student-t arm in any world. The compound gates as constituted test the registered scale law, not the challenger. The reviewer's concern about compound gates being dominated by dispersion is confirmed and quantified.
design_finding_1_compound_gates_are_non_.what_this_says_about_EXP001B: its M0/M1 intervals were narrower than nominal by construction. This does NOT change its verdict: the paired M1-M0 comparison shared the same k, so the comparison was fair. It does mean 'beating the EXP-001B baseline' on log-likelihood is a low bar that any correctly scaled model clears.
design_finding_1_compound_gates_are_non_.proposal_for_review_NOT_applied: either (a) redefine G2/G3 against SCALE-MATCHED versions of M0/M1 (same mean laws, Gaussian, with sd from ML on fit-split residuals), so the compound gates test mean and shape rather than an estimator artifact, or (b) drop the replacement verdict and report the registered comparisons as compound context only. Registered M0 and M1 themselves stay untouched either way.

design_finding_2_inference_disagreement_.observation: HAC and the session bootstrap disagreed on M1-M0 and L-S in W1 and on C-L in W3 (bootstrap p=0.0476 vs threshold 0.0228 borderline); sensitivity block lengths 1 and 10 also disagreed with 5 on the W1 pairs
design_finding_2_inference_disagreement_.reading: on this synthetic process the session bootstrap is the more permissive of the two near t~2. The disagreement rule held and produced the declared verdict. Whether the bootstrap is anti-conservative here or HAC conservative is not established by one realisation.
